title: Internal Hom from a locally finitely presented module preserves filtered colimits
statement: Let C be a category with objects in universe u+1 and morphisms in u, equipped with a Grothendieck topology J. Assume abelian sheafification in universe u+1 exists and that J-equivalences are exactly locally bijective maps on J, all slice sites J/U, and all iterated slice sites (J/U)/W. Assume composition with the forgetful functor from commutative rings to rings preserves sheaves on J and all J/U. For a sheaf A of commutative rings and an A-module sheaf P [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] which locally admits a finite presentation, internalHom_A(P,-) [def-pur-sheaf-hom] preserves every small filtered colimit of A-module sheaves indexed in universe u+1.

proof.text: Use IsFinitePresentation.exists_quasicoherentData to obtain a covering family Xi and a finite global presentation of P.over Xi. Restriction over Xi preserves colimits because underlying abelian slice restriction is a left adjoint; the proved module forgetful theorem preserves and reflects these colimits.

Identify (internalHom(P,N)).over U with internalHom(P.over U,N.over U), naturally in N. Use the componentwise identity isomorphism from the actual restriction to pure presheaf restriction, followed by PresheafOfModules.restrictOverHomObjIso, which uses the equivalence between iterated slice categories.

Apply the finite global presentation theorem to the restricted diagram on every Xi. The restriction-colimit comparison and the preceding natural isomorphism imply that the restriction of colimit.post N internalHom(P,-) is an isomorphism for every Xi.

Restrictions to the covering family jointly detect isomorphisms. At any object mapping into Xi, evaluation of the restricted isomorphism makes the underlying component bijective. The covering sieve of objects mapping into some Xi therefore witnesses local surjectivity and local injectivity of the underlying abelian sheaf map. A locally bijective sheaf map is an isomorphism, and the module forgetful functor reflects this isomorphism. Thus the original colimit comparison is an isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem internalHom_preserves_filteredColimit_of_isFinitePresentation
    {C : Type (u + 1)} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})]
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}]
    [∀ U, HasSheafify (J.over U) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}]
    [∀ U, (J.over U).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}]
    [∀ U W, HasSheafify ((J.over U).over W) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}]
    [∀ U W, ((J.over U).over W).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}]
    [∀ U, (J.over U).HasSheafCompose
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})]
    (A : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (P : SheafOfModules.{u + 1}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat.{u + 1})).obj A))
    [P.IsFinitePresentation]
    (I : Type (u + 1)) [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I]
    (N : I ⥤ SheafOfModules.{u + 1}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat.{u + 1})).obj A)) :
    PreservesColimit N ((homFunctor A).obj (op P))
